successors.name: British Raj
successors.text: Kengtung and its substates (Hsenyawt, Hsenmawng, Monghsat, Mongpu): the Shan state east of the Salween, 31,079 km2 in 1901

ledger.x: c. 1243: Mang Kun, a delegate of King Mangrai, founds Kengtung ('Tai Khuen City'). 'Founded around 1243 by a prince named Mang Kun'; the Wa people 'were displaced around 1229'; the Chinese list dates Mang Kun to 1263, and the infobox gives the dynasty's establishment as '3 May' with no year.
1814: the Kengtung dynasty is restored with Burmese help and Mongyawng annexed.
1895: the state is counted as ended.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1849-1855)
wars.outcome: Kengtung-Konbaung victory: Lanna forces (1850) and Bangkok armies (1852-54) laid siege to Kengtung on 10 March 1853, retreated on 23 March 1853, and withdrew again in March 1854; Siam gained neither Kengtung nor Chiang Hung.

certainty.note: The only dimensions are the 1901 area and the substates' names; no frontier is given.
